NutriCorp Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCorp Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a telephone, or click the Q&A button in the webcast interface if joining online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCorp Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Jamie.

Jamie Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: performance in key channels including retail, foodservice, and convenience; our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies; the impact of new product innovations and launches; gross margin analysis including drivers and trends; our capital expenditure plans and priorities; and EPS guidance along with key assumptions.

First, regarding performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, and convenience: we drove top-line growth with retail up double-digits, convenience surging, and foodservice holding steady amid traffic challenges.

Second, concerning discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: our disciplined approach delivered solid net pricing realization while protecting volumes through targeted promotions and premium mix shifts.

Third, in terms of impact of new product innovations and launches: these contributed significantly to growth, with functional beverages and plant-based snacks leading the way and high repeat rates.

Fourth, looking at gross margin analysis: drivers and trends: we expanded margins through pricing, efficiencies, and mix, more than offsetting commodity headwinds.

Fifth, reviewing capital expenditure plans and priorities: we're investing strategically in capacity, automation, and resilience to support long-term growth.

Sixth, analyzing EPS guidance and key assumptions: our outlook reflects balanced growth across revenue, margins, and disciplined spending.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to provide more detail on our financial results and expand on these areas.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Jamie. As Jamie mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $6.5 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.5%, impacted by a favorable mix and efficiencies that outweighed commodity inflation. Operating income was $1.25 billion, and adjusted earnings per share were $0.85. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted EPS of $3.45 to $3.55.

Let me now expand on the six key areas Jamie highlighted, starting with our performance across key channels: retail, foodservice, and convenience, which collectively drove our top-line growth of 8% year-over-year to $6.5 billion. This resilience comes amid persistent inflationary pressures on commodities like cocoa, dairy, and edible oils, which have risen 15-20% globally per the USDA's latest ag outlook, and softer consumer sentiment in certain segments. We've offset this through disciplined pricing—up 6.5% average across the portfolio—while protecting household penetration via targeted promotions and everyday low pricing strategies.

Retail, which accounted for 62% of our sales or about $4 billion, up 12.4% reported and 9.8% organic, remains our growth engine, fueled by sustained at-home consumption trends post-pandemic. Grocery drove over half of retail volume, with dollar sales up 14% in multi-outlet scanning, outpacing the category average of 7% per IRI. Our flagship brands like CrunchTime Snacks and PureSip Beverages saw velocity gains of 8-10% in key banners—think Kroger, Albertsons, and Publix—thanks to expanded all-commodity volume distribution. We hit 92% ACV for CrunchTime's new high-protein bar line, up from 65% last quarter, capturing share from legacy players like Clif Bar and KIND.

Club channels were a standout, contributing 22% of retail growth with 18% comps, led by Sam's Club and Costco reloads on our family-pack frozen pizzas and RTD protein shakes. Basket size here expanded 5%, as consumers traded up to our premium NutriBoost line amid health halo demands—low-sugar, plant-based SKUs that align with the 25% YoY surge in functional beverage demand per Mintel. E-commerce, now 15% of retail, grew 28%, with strong Amazon performance via Subscribe & Save and Walmart+ integrations. Regionally, U.S. Northeast and Midwest led at 14% growth on back-to-school replenishment, while international retail in Europe—via Tesco and Carrefour—dipped 2% due to UK volume softness from excise taxes on sugary drinks, prompting us to accelerate zero-sugar reformulations.

Strategically, we've invested $45 million in shelf resets and planogram optimizations, securing 12% more linear feet in the snack aisle. Our tech initiatives include AI-driven assortment planning with NielsenIQ, which boosted facings for high-margin items by 15%, and blockchain traceability for our organic lines to appeal to Gen Z shoppers scanning QR codes for provenance.

Shifting to foodservice, 24% of total sales at $1.56 billion, which was flat YoY on a 2% organic decline. This channel faced headwinds from labor shortages—restaurant traffic down 3% per Black Box Intelligence—and menu price fatigue, with QSR check averages up only 1.5% despite 7% food-away-from-home inflation. Quick-service restaurants like McDonald's and Taco Bell, which make up 40% of our foodservice mix, saw mid-single-digit declines as operators dialed back protein costs amid avian flu disruptions. Our value-engineered tenders and sauces held share but volumes softened 4%.

Conversely, casual dining and table service rebounded 5%, with Chili's and Applebee's chains reloading on our app-based bundle packs—think loaded nacho kits that support their shareable menu pivots. Institutional lagged at -1%, pressured by school budget constraints, though healthcare grew 8% on premium grab-and-go yogurt parfaits for hospital cafeterias. Regionally, U.S. Sunbelt strength offset Midwest weakness, while Latin America—via Sysco and US Foods partnerships—surged 11% on Mexico City quickserve expansion.

Key initiatives here include our Operator Portal 2.0, a digital platform with real-time inventory forecasting and customized recipe APIs, reducing stockouts by 22% and boosting repeat orders 15%. We've also launched co-branded limited-time offers with Yum! Brands, driving 20% uplift in trial for our spicy sriracha dips. Looking ahead, we're targeting 5-7% growth in FY24 by leaning into ghost kitchens and delivery aggregators like DoorDash, where our packaged sides grew 25% quarter-over-quarter.

Finally, convenience, our highest-growth channel at 14% of sales or $910 million, up 15.7% YoY and 13% organic. C-stores remain a bright spot, with footfall rebounding 6% per NACS data, driven by on-the-go snacking amid hybrid work. 7-Eleven, Circle K, and Wawa accounted for 60% of volume, where our roller grill franks and single-serve energy drinks posted 20%+ gains. Private label erosion in this channel—down 2 points per Circana—opened doors for our QuickBite meal kits, now in 75% of top-100 c-stores.

Fuel and tobacco adjacency sales boosted basket rings, with our combo deals (drink + snack) lifting average transaction value 7% to $4.82. Trends like better-for-you indulgences shone through: low-carb pretzels up 30%, tapping the 18% category growth in healthier convenience per Datassential. Regionally, Southeast U.S. flew at 19% on travel recovery, while Canada convenience grew 12% despite softer gas demand.

We've doubled down on technical plays: vending machine services integrations with Nayax for cashless payments, expanding to 5,000 machines, and micro-fulfillment pilots with Gopuff for same-hour delivery. Pricing discipline—4% hikes masked by value tiers—preserved margins at 28.5%, up 50 bps.

In summary for channels, the mix shift toward retail and convenience—now 76% of portfolio—delivered 520 bps of margin expansion to 22.4%, with gross margins hitting 36.8% ex-FX. This reflects our Channel Excellence strategy: $120 million in capex for cold-chain upgrades, reducing on-time in-full misses to 97%, and a robust innovation pipeline with 25 new SKUs launching Q4, including plant-based nuggets for foodservice and electrolyte pouches for convenience. We've gained 110 bps of market share overall in core categories per Nielsen and IRI, with household penetration at all-time highs and 4.5 months of channel inventory positioning us for 7-9% organic growth in FY24.

Next, on our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, which have been the cornerstone of our 8% organic revenue growth this quarter, outpacing the broader Food & Beverage industry where NielsenIQ pegs category growth at 4.1% globally. Q3 organic net revenue grew 8%, comprising 4.8 percentage points from net pricing, 1.7 points from favorable mix shift, and 1.5 points from volume. Year-to-date, this translates to 7.5% organic growth, with pricing contributing a robust 4.5 points. Our average selling price across the portfolio rose 5.2% year-over-year, reflecting disciplined execution amid persistent input cost inflation. Gross inflation on key commodities like sugar, cocoa, and vegetable oils hovered around 8-10% globally per the FAO Food Price Index, but our RGM discipline kept net material value pass-through at about 60%, preserving healthy margins.

We implemented targeted list price increases averaging 6.1% across our portfolio since Q4 2023, phased strategically to minimize volume elasticity impacts. In beverages, 45% of revenue, we took a 6.5% increase on carbonated soft drinks like our AgriFizz line and 5.8% on juices and functional waters. This was calibrated based on proprietary consumer elasticity modeling, showing -2.3 average for CSDs but -1.8 for premium functionals. Net pricing realization hit 5.1% in beverages, with volumes flat offset by 2.1% mix uplift from premiumization—our AgriFizz Zero Sugar now 15% of CSD sales.

In snacks and confectionery, 35% of revenue, pricing was 7.2% on chocolate-coated products amid cocoa spiking 45% YTD to $10,000 per metric ton, yielding 5.9% net and 1.2% volume growth. Savory snacks like AgriCrunch chips saw 4.5% to protect share against Lay's and Oreo extensions. Dairy and plant-based alternatives, 20% of revenue, had 5.3% pricing, with plant-based milks gaining 3.2% volumes on sustainability trends.

We've optimized trade spend to 18.2% of revenue from 19.7% last year via our Trade Promotion Effectiveness dashboard with AI from Nielsen and PROS partnerships, shifting to loyalty-focused EDLP on hero SKUs and lifting promotion ROI by 22%.

Our RGM pyramid—volume base, mix middle, pricing apex—delivered through premiumization: premium products now 28% of revenue, up from 22%. Functional hydration like AgriHydrate grew 14%, savory nuts and protein bars 18%. Innovation launched 12 new items in H1, contributing 2.3% growth with 140% repeat rates; packaging like lighter PET bottles cut freight 8%.

Regionally, North America (55% revenue) saw 5.6% net pricing, EMEA 4.2% prioritizing volume, APAC 8.1% with China premiumization, LATAM 6.7%. Our Revenue Growth Management Center with SAP and Blue Yonder runs weekly scenarios, replacing static cycles. We'll maintain 4-5% pricing into 2025 for 5-7% organic growth.

Turning to the impact of new product innovations and launches, a key growth engine in an industry shifting toward health, sustainability, and premiumization—validated by NielsenIQ's 12% rise in functional beverages and 18% in plant-based SKUs. New products, launches within 12 months, generated $850 million in Q3 net revenue, 14% of total top-line growth and 42% YoY increase from prior year. This outpaced core brands at 7%, with gross margins on new items at 52%, 450 bps above company average, from optimized formulations.

Standout: VitaBoost functional beverage line—zero-sugar, adaptogen-infused sparkling water launched February, leveraging nootropics like lion's mane for focus. $360 million Q3 sales, 28% velocity in Walmart/Kroger, 65% repeat rates via AI app with Instacart. Snacks: GreenHarvest plant-based protein bars with upcycled pea protein and fermented dairy alternatives, $285 million sales, 22% share gains in high-protein, EBITDA 28% from regenerative sourcing cutting COGS 11%.

North America 62% of new sales at $530 million, 18% growth; EMEA $190 million, 22%; APAC $95 million, 51%; LATAM $40 million, 29%. $250 million annual R&D, Innovation Flywheel with consumer insights, rapid prototyping in Singapore, agile GTM. 85% new SKUs rPET packaging, top-10 DJSI spot, NPS to 72. Pipeline: probiotic soda, upcycled chips; expect 16-18% FY25 contribution.

On gross margin analysis: drivers and trends, we delivered 38.5% consolidated, up 230 bps YoY from 36.2% and 110 bps sequentially from Q2's 37.4%. Sixth straight quarter of expansion from pricing discipline, mix optimization, efficiencies amid volatile inputs.

Positives: 350 bps tailwinds. Pricing and mix +280 bps: 9% actions, beverages 11% on NutriGlow kombucha +45%; premium/health SKUs 32% sales vs 25%, OatFlex +28%, NutriBars +22%. Supply chain efficiencies +120 bps: NutriChain 2.0 AI/blockchain cut waste 15%, inventory 8%; 70% FY25 commodities hedged; BayNut acquisition shaved 4% almond COGS.

Headwinds 120 bps: commodities -90 bps, cocoa +42% to $10k/mt on indulgence; dairy +12%. Mitigated 60% via swaps/West Africa. Logistics/FX -30 bps, freight +22% Red Sea, nearshoring Mexico 40% NA production.

Regions: NA 42% rev, 40.1% margin +320 bps; EMEA 28%, 36.8%; APAC/LATAM 30%, 37.2% +180 bps. 12-month trailing 37.8% vs industry 33.3%, ahead of peers.

Trends: inflation cooling to 2-4%; levers: portfolio reshaping (divest low-margin), robotics for 5% COGS cut FY26, sustainable sourcing 80% coffee/tea certified. Q4 guide 39.0-39.5%, FY25 39.5-40.0%.

Now, capital expenditure plans and priorities for FY25 reflect disciplined investing for mid-teens ROIC amid 8% YoY commodity inflation on cocoa/coffee/oils, labor shortages, ESG mandates. Laser-focused on capacity for high-margin, efficiency via digital/automation, supply chain resilience.

FY25 capex $1.2B, +15% from $1.05B FY24, 4.5% of $26.5B sales, funded from >$2.5B op cash flow, 12% ROIC hurdle, 85% payback 3-4 years, in line with PepsiCo/Mondelez.

Manufacturing/capacity 45% $540M: $250M NA retrofit Chicago/Dallas aseptic lines for VitaFuel +25% capacity, 8% Q3 bev growth; $150M APAC Vietnam greenfield RTD teas/low-sugar juices; $100M EMEA Rotterdam sustainable PET -40% virgin resin, SBTi net-zero 2040.

Efficiency/automation 30% $360M: $200M robotic palletizers/AI QC Rockwell 15 plants, 15% conversion cut like General Mills; digital twins Siemens for CrunchVita pulse chips; $50M precision fermentation Perfect Day dairy-free creamers, alt-protein.

Supply chain/distribution 15% $180M: $100M micro-fulfillment Mexico/India AutoStore D2C e-comm 40% delivery cut; $80M LATAM cold chain El Niño fruits 2-8°C.

Innovation/IT/corporate 10% $120M: SAP S/4HANA real-time inventory, AI forecasting -20% stockouts.

De-risks to premiumization: health/wellness 35% sales +10 pts, sustainability 22% growth, EM 28% by FY27. Avoids low-ROIC carbs. Delivers 10-12% organic, 200 bps margin, ROIC accretion.

Finally, EPS guidance and key assumptions: FY25 adjusted EPS $3.45-$3.55, 8-11% growth midpoint over FY24 $3.20, above Street $3.48. Q4 $0.95-$1.05, 7-15% YoY, sequential from Q3 $0.85 on holiday volumes.

Organic revenue 5-7%, 60% pricing 3-4%, 40% volume/mix 1-2%. NA 4% on hydration +12%, premium RTD coffee; Europe 6-8% plant-based +25%; EM 28% portfolio, 9-11% urbanization India +18%, Mexico resilient.

Gross margin +120-150 bps to 42.5-43.0%, $250M productivity Supply Chain 2.0 AI routing -8% freight, precision ag; commodities 2-3% vs 6%, 80% hedged, cocoa wildcard -50 bps chocolate shakes.

Op ex +4-5% or 100 bps sales, $150M digital/R&D/sustainability; op margin 18.5-19.0% +80 bps. Tax 23.5%, interest $120M, net debt $1.2B 2.2x EBITDA, $800M repurchases +$0.05 EPS.

Risks: inflation surprises $100M contingency, consumer spending; upside premium mix, port resolution. Embeds Health Forward: 60% pipeline low/no-sugar/functional, $200B wellness market 7% CAGR.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Jamie Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, John. Inflation remains a challenge, particularly on cocoa up 42% and dairy 12%, but we've mitigated through 9% pricing actions realizing full benefits, hedging 70-80% of volumes, nearshoring, and alternate sourcing like West Africa. This, combined with efficiencies from NutriChain 2.0 cutting waste 15%, allowed 230 bps gross margin expansion. We're positioned well as inflation cools to 2-4%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for VitaBoost and what is the expected revenue impact?

Mike Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. VitaBoost, our zero-sugar adaptogen sparkling water, is off to a strong start with $360 million Q3 sales and 28% velocity growth in major retailers. Plans include expanding to 95% ACV by year-end via club and e-comm, localized flavors for APAC/EMEA, and AI personalization for repeats at 65%. We expect it to contribute 5-7% to FY25 revenue growth, with 52% margins from efficient formulations and regenerative sourcing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

David Lee (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Lisa Chen (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. Post-Red Sea with freight +30%, we're enhancing resilience via $180 million capex: two automated micro-fulfillment centers in Mexico/India cutting delivery 40% for e-comm, cold chain upgrades LATAM for fruits, hedging 80% wheat/corn, nearshoring 40% NA production, and blockchain/AI forecasting reducing stockouts 20%. OTIF at 97%, positioning us for volatility like El Niño.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Rachel Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thanks, Rachel. For Q4, we see continued momentum with organic growth 6-8%, gross margins 39-39.5%, EPS $0.95-1.05. Full-year reaffirms 5-7% revenue growth, margin expansion, mid-teens EPS growth. Key: moderating inflation, premium mix, new products 16% contribution, capex leverage. Risks hedged, upside from efficiencies and EM.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Jamie for closing remarks.

Jamie Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCorp Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
